blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-performance-1 (One customer query per invoice (N+1)) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: `customer_label` runs `db.customer(invoice.customer_id)` (src/report.rs:39), i.e. `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1`, once per invoice: about 3 000 queries for a month of 3 000 invoices from 800 customers, growing linearly with the month's invoices. Collect the distinct `customer_id`s, load them in one call with the existing `Db::customers(&[i64])` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`, src/db.rs:26), index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>` and build each label from it. Keep the current error behavior when a customer is missing (return a `DbError`) and the invoice-number order.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice (N+1)

findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for every invoice of the month (src/report.rs:28), so the pattern is compiled about 3 000 times per report, cost growing with the number of invoices, while it never changes. Compile it once — a `static` `std::sync::OnceLock<Regex>` (or `LazyLock`), or build it in `monthly_report` before the loop and pass it to `purchase_order`.
findings.title: Purchase-order regex compiled once per invoice
